q: The greatest griefs are those we cause ourselves.
To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all.
Only a moment you stayed, but what an imprint your footprints have left on our hearts.
It matters not how a man dies, but how he lives.
How wonderful it is that nobody need wait a single moment before starting to improve the world.
Goodbyes are only for those who love with their eyes. Because for those who love with heart and soul there is no such thing as separation.
The heart that has truly loved never forgets.
Love is a fabric which never fades, no matter how often it is washed in the water of adversity and grief.
The life of the dead is placed in the memory of the living.
Those we love and lose are always connected by heartstrings into infinity.
If you would be loved, love, and be loveable.
The only way to have a friend is to be one.
Love is composed of a single soul inhabiting two bodies.
A parting is a beautiful sorrow.
In the arithmetic of love, one plus one equals everything, and two minus one equals nothing.
There is no charm equal to tenderness of heart.
Memory is a way of holding on to the things you love, the things you are, the things you never want to lose.
They that love beyond the world cannot be separated by it.
Death leaves a heartache no one can heal, love leaves a memory no one can steal.
Where there is deep grief, there was great love.
Sometimes you will never know the value of a moment, until it becomes a memory.
Life is a beautiful magnificent thing, even to a jellyfish.
A true friend is one soul in two bodies.
We loved with a love that was more than love.
For life and death are one, even as the river and the sea are one.
Digital minimalism definitively does not reject the innovations of the internet age, but instead rejects the way so many people currently engage with these tools.
The urge to check Twitter or refresh Reddit becomes a nervous twitch that shatters uninterrupted time into shards too small to support the presence necessary for an intentional life.
You cannot expect an app dreamed up in a dorm room to successfully replace the types of rich interactions to which we have painstakingly adapted over millennia.
Digital minimalists see new technologies as tools to be used to support things they deeply value, not as sources of value themselves.
All of humanity's problems stem from man's inability to sit quietly in a room alone.
I fear the day that technology will surpass our human interaction. The world will have a generation of idiots.
The more you connect with your phone, the less you connect with your soul.
It is entirely possible that behind the screens, we are all hiding from the beautiful reality of being present.
Minimalists don't mind missing out on small things; what worries them much more is diminishing the large things they already know for sure make a good life good.
Disconnect to connect.
If you are constantly staring at a screen, you will miss the breathtaking canvas of the sky.
Real conversation takes time, and the total number of people for which you can uphold this standard will be significantly less than the total number of people you can follow.
There is a very real zero-sum relationship between online and offline interaction.
Do not let your digital life become a substitute for your physical life.
A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.
Look up, the best moments are happening right in front of you, not inside a screen.
True connection is felt in the heart, not measured in a follower count.
You are not missing out on anything online that is more important than the life happening around you right now.
Put down the device and pick up your life.
Technology should improve your life, not become your life.
Solitude deprivation is a state in which you spend close to zero time alone with your own thoughts and free from input from other minds.
Your smartphone is a tool, do not let it turn you into its tool.
Be in control of your tech, do not let it control your time.
We live in a world that is working to eliminate touch as one of our senses, to minimize the use of our hands to do things except poke at a screen.
Real conversation takes time.
Gratitude is not a passive response to something we have been given, gratitude is being awake in the presence of everything that lives within and without us.
Let us be entirely thankful for the present moment, because right now is the only place life exists.
Gratitude and attitude are not challenges; they are choices.
What separates privilege from entitlement is gratitude.
Gratitude turns what we have into enough.
If you want to find happiness, find gratitude.
A noble person is mindful and thankful of the favors he receives from others.
This is a wonderful day. I have never seen this one before.
When we focus on our gratitude, the tide of disappointment goes out and the tide of love rushes in.
Be mindful. Be grateful. Be positive. Be true. Be kind.
We often take for granted the very things that most deserve our gratitude.
Gratitude paints little smiley faces on everything it touches.
When it comes to life the critical thing is whether you take things for granted or take them with gratitude.
In all affairs it is a healthy thing now and then to hang a question mark on the things you have long taken for granted.
O Lord that lends me life, lend me a heart replete with thankfulness.
Happiness cannot be traveled to, owned, earned, worn or consumed. Happiness is the spiritual experience of living every minute with love, grace, and gratitude.
Things turn out best for people who make the best of the way things turn out.
Gratitude builds a bridge to abundance.
Give thanks for a little and you will find a lot.
Gratitude is the fairest blossom which springs from the soul.
If you concentrate on finding whatever is good in every situation, you will discover that your life will suddenly be filled with gratitude, a feeling that nurtures the soul.
Gratitude is a quality similar to electricity: it must be produced and discharged and used up in order to exist at all.
Reflect upon your present blessings, of which every man has plenty; not on your past misfortunes, of which all men have some.
Be thankful for everything that happens in your life; it is all an experience.
Nothing is more honorable than a grateful heart.
A person's success should be measured by their own inner scorecard, not the validation of a crowd.
I care not what others think of what I do, but I care very much about what I think of what I do. That is character.
Whatever you do, do it for yourself, not for the validation of the world.
The most exhausting thing in life is being insincere.
A man cannot be comfortable without his own approval.
To be nobody but yourself in a world which is doing its best, night and day, to make you everybody else means to fight the hardest battle.
A truly strong person does not need the approval of others any more than a lion needs the approval of sheep.
You have been criticizing yourself for years, and it hasn't worked. Try approving of yourself and see what happens.
Do not look for approval except for the consciousness of doing your best.
The only permission you need to live a brilliant life is your own.
A tiger does not lose sleep over the opinion of sheep.
Seek respect, not attention. It lasts longer.
Once you embrace your value, talents, and strengths, it neutralizes when others think less of you.
Stop looking outside for what can only be found inside.
Make sure you don't start seeing yourself through the eyes of those who don't value you.
Care about your own opinion first; the rest is just background noise.
The reward for conformity is that everyone likes you except yourself.
Some people say you are going the wrong way, when it is simply a way of your own.
You are the only one who gets to decide what you are worth.
Authenticity is a collection of choices that we have to make every day. It is about the choice to show up and be real.
If you figure out who you are and you stay true to yourself, you don't need anyone's validation.
We must not allow other people's limited perceptions to define us.
Why should we worry about what others think of us, do we have more confidence in their opinions than we do our own?
Be who you are and say what you feel, because those who mind don't matter, and those who matter don't mind.
The inner scoreboard is about eliminating comparison with others and living in alignment with what is most important to you.
